summary:
# NOTES: LOVE AND THE IRONMONGER (F. J. Randall, 1908, John Lane, London/NY)
Subtitle: "A Plain Tale of Upper Thames Street." Gutenberg #45598. Single book, no separate volumes.

## Front matter / ads
Title page: John Lane, The Bodley Head; NY: John Lane Co., MCMVIII. Printed by William Clowes & Sons. Contents lists 25 chapters (I–XXV). Back matter is a publisher's catalogue of other novels (e.g., "The Judgment of Paris" by M. P. Willcocks, "Absolution" by Clara Viebig, Grant Allen, George Egerton, Richard Le Gallienne, etc.); its blurb for this book says a junior clerk blackmails the legatees and "the blackmailed turn on the blackmailer."

## Chapter I – What came to George Early through a Keyhole
- Offices of Fairbrother & Co., Upper Thames Street, iron trade. George Early arrives 8:30, late. Head clerk Thomas Parrott ("Polly") scolds. Shorthand clerk, red-haired junior, Matthews (freckled youth) present.
- Old Joe (Joseph Fairbrother), head of firm, unwell, "one foot in grave." George hides in tiny room off private staircase; watches through keyhole.
- Fairbrother tells Parrott he has a legacy: £500/yr for life if he stops meanness (must lend when asked; lawyer monitors; three warnings before loss). Parrott is mean "by habit."
- Then interviews Albert Busby (cashier, under 40, compulsive liar; £500/yr if he stops lying) and Jimmy Gray (accountant, drink problem; £500/yr to quit drink). Three legatees, same conditions structure.
- George exclaims "Well, I'm hanged!"

## Chapter II – A Young Man in search of Bad Habits
- George tries to find a vice to win legacy. Tries borrowing (rejected as weak), swearing (learned from Billingsgate porter; sailor at saloon of inn).
- Asks Gray about Flower-of-the-Field racing tip; offers Scotch from desk, Gray refuses.
- Busby: George reveals knowledge of Busby's sister-in-law "Fanny" secret; Busby admits lie.
- George borrows half-crown from Parrott (first loan).
- Next morning George swears loudly; Busby announces Old Joe is dead.

## Chapter III – George Early proves that Knowledge is Power
- Miss Ellen Fairbrother (22, from Australia; lived with aunt Phoebe) becomes head; takes residence at Brunswick Terrace, West End, Kensington.
- Parrott moves to small ground-floor office. George borrows five shillings; Parrott lends.
- George blackmails Gray at Gray's lunch restaurant (half-sovereign); tells Gray he knows.
- Follows Busby to Clapham (corner house, Free Library, billiard saloon). Meets Mrs. Fanny Busby; Busby lied to wife about library. George pretends knowledge of legacy ("Old Joe's will"); Busby begs silence. George insists on supper; borrows half-sovereign for cab.

## Chapter IV – Three Worms that turned
- George late to breakfast; landlady Mrs. Haskins; maid Carrie. Says "rabbit for dinner."
- Office: Matthews. George blackmails Gray; Gray meets George at public-house alley near Queen Victoria St; threatens; George has notebook.
- Busby's wife Fanny goes to mother's (ten-pound note from Busby). Parrott refuses George 5 shillings; offers eightpence.
- George pretends meek; "Sir" to Parrott.

## Chapter V – A New Lodger in Leytonstone
- Gray meets old pal Charles Lambert ("Society of Old Friends," secretary post £60/yr, guinea membership). Gray tells wife Emily (Mrs. Gray) he's secretary; she has let front room to a lodger, George Early (£1/week, full board). Gray is sick of George.
- George lodges with Grays in Leytonstone villa. Gray tells George "not a word."
- Parrott dismisses George (set at liberty a week). George counters: wants promotion. Result: George made secretary to Miss Fairbrother.
- Old Josh (carman Benson) asks Parrott for £5 loan.

## Chapter VI – Lamb Chops and Tomato Sauce
- Parrott's fiancée Lucy Perkins (milliner, Paddington; mother Mrs. Perkins has £2000). Wednesday dinner at Mrs. Carey's lodging house.
- George visits, Parrott hides in clothes-cupboard. George and Lucy eat lamb chops, drink claret; flirt; George mocks Parrott. Parrott emerges. George: "If you don't sit... I'll borrow ten pounds!"

## Chapter VII – An Erring Husband improves against his Will
- George secretary to Miss Fairbrother; visitor Joseph Brown, builder, knew her as toddler.
- Gray pays George to reveal Busby's secret: £5 (George told him "Busby is liar; Gray is man who knows" secret—actually George says the secret is Busby's vice of being not reformed).
- Mrs. Gray buys bookshelf at Stratford sale; meets Mrs. Busby (same bookshelf rivalry). Mrs. Busby tells of Busby's Free Library habit; Mrs. Busby recalled to Clapham.

## Chapter VIII – George Early holds Fortune in his Arms
- Gray follows Busby; Busby slips on orange-peel; Gray warns "Gray is the man who knows."
- George and Gray's £5 deal; Gray pays George. George dines at Café Royal.
- Regent Street: George rescues Miss Fairbrother from hansom accident; holds her in arms.
- George meets Busby (smoking concert). Busby drunk, reveals Gray's secret; George "swaps" vices. Busby plans to tickle Parrott/Gray.

## Chapter IX – The Man who laughed Last and Loudest
- Busby refuses to lend Gray money; Gray refuses Busby ten shillings. Busby and Gray conspire against George; Parrott joins (Parrott drinks; Busby knows).
- George enters Parrott's office; Miss Fairbrother's letter gives George authority.
- Miss Fairbrother's letter: "DEAR MR. PARROTT..."; George in charge while she's away.

## Chapter X – Hero Worship
- Miss Fairbrother's second note invites George to Brunswick Terrace. George flirts; she pours tea; hand-holding; George moves into West End lodgings.

## Chapter XI – Cupid takes a Hand
- Upper Thames Street narrative: lunchers Henry Cacklin (junior clerk, 16) and William (Billy) Budd (office-boy); café; they gossip about George and Miss Fairbrother; Cacklin bets £1 George marries her.

## Chapter XII – An Ironmonger in Love
- George and Ellen friendship. Hampton Court river trip by steamer from Westminster; first kiss in grass; that night Trocadero, then "Good night, my darling." / "Good night, George dear."

## Chapter XIII – A Fortnight's Holiday
- Engagement; Aunt Phoebe interviews George; he refuses to discuss property ("Do what you like with it").
- Married; honeymoon on Continent (fortnight). Parrott plans Streatham/Upper Tooting. Mrs. Gray: "Poor old George!" Gray drinks again; claims "club secretary" to wife; she weeps.

## Chapter XIV – "Tommy Morgan"
- George runs firm as proprietor; lectures Gray.
- Dibbs & Dubbs (law firm, St. Paul's Passage, Queen Victoria St.); new lawyer Dawkins (son-in-law of Dubbs). Clerk Mole sent on sleuth mission; follows Gray to restaurant (Cannon Street); fake whisky "Tommy Morgan" from "Blue Crown"; promises free bottle. Mrs. Gray: "unlucky to meet a man named Mole on a Friday."

## Chapter XV – Aunt Phoebe surprises her Nephew
- Mrs. Early superstitions (salt, knives, spoon = stranger). Aunt Phoebe coming to stay. Martha the maid.
- Blue warning letter (Dibbs & Dubbs) to Gray: first warning. Gray lost secretaryship; Mrs. Gray believes "Mould" libelled him.
- Gray drinks at Stratford, meets Mole; chases him.
- Aunt Phoebe reveals: Gray's legacy reverts to George if lost; if George loses it, Ellen's fortune goes to charities. George: "SILLY OLD FOOL!"

## Chapter XVI – George Early and the Giant Alcohol
- George frantic; Gray missing. Visits Mrs. Gray pretending Gray drinks, is affectionate with "Flora", "Alice", "May", "Chrissy"; she vows to smash whisky bottles.
- Gray's second blue warning. George becomes teetotaler. Lawyer says "Very Dark African Mission" benefits from estate.

## Chapter XVII – Advice Gratis
- Gray: "burying grandmother"/"out with Flora." George posts texts (George Washington portrait). Office boy Bailey (cousin of Matthews).
- Busby and Parrott receive blue warnings. Busby's card-carrying stranger; Busby tells Dibbs & Dubbs George not there.
- George leaves office; Mole follows him. Aunt Phoebe interrogates George about Sunday School and rescued lives.
- George resolves: "I'll try being good."

## Chapter XVIII – The Disadvantages of trying to be Good
- George offers "Friendly Friday Evenings for Mothers Society" £10 subscription. Gray demands £5 loan; George delays.
- Gas-stove customer (Mr. unnamed) tricks George into admitting Fairbrother pamphlet lies; George overhears Gray, Busby, Parrott plotting £100 each.

## Chapter XIX – A Shot that missed Fire
- Conspirators plot to ambush George at office; Aunt Phoebe chaperones. Gray visits Dawkins: says George forfeited 2 legacies; George only temperance remains.

## Chapter XX – A Dark Man of Foreign Appearance
- Caroli (dark foreign man with friend) tricks George into whisky via mesmerism at showroom. Gray follows Caroli. Aunt Phoebe finds George in wine-shop.

## Chapter XXI – Follow my Leader
- George escapes to Victoria, then country inn Wheatsheaf (landlord). Telegram from Ellen: "discharged all three." Gray comes to inn; George escapes via window; tricks Gray; takes trap to station; train; detained as "suspicious character" in cloak-room; burns room with paper; fire.

## Chapter XXII – Blind Man's Bluff
- Fire scare; George escapes, climbs tree; Gray offers five pounds; branch breaks. Vicar (country parson) and daughter; George feigns deafness and blindness. Doctor John Cattermole (Walworth chemist) takes him to Sevenoaks.

## Chapter XXIII – First Stop, Hastings
- Inn on hill; waitress; cook Mrs. Baily; George feigns insanity; Gray, Parrott, Busby pursue. Landlady's lost son "Erny"/"Moggles" — George claimed as her son. Albert (twin). George swaps clothes with Albert; escapes. "First stop, Hastings."

## Chapter XXIV – A Strawberry Mark
- George in London; meets cousin Tops (Ellen's cousin from Australia, Mrs. Early's actual name is Babs). Tops is Miss Ellen; Mrs. Early is cousin "Babs" — Ellen Fairbrother's twin cousin with strawberry mark on arm: Mrs. Early (Babs) has strawberry birthmark = John Fairbrother's daughter; true heiress. Aunt Phoebe's revelation.

## Chapter XXV – Name o' Phoebe
- Cattermole and George on Elephant bus: George reveals intention to name child Phoebe; cousin inherits fortune; George and Cattermole's conversation; closing.

# Key people
George Early (protagonist, later "Georgy-Porgy"); Joseph Fairbrother ("Old Joe"); Thomas Parrott (head clerk, "Polly"); Albert Busby (cashier, wife Fanny); Jimmy Gray (accountant, wife Emily/"Em"); Miss Ellen Fairbrother (later Mrs. Early); Aunt Phoebe; Mrs. Haskins; Carrie; Matthews; Mrs. Carey; Lucy Perkins; Mrs. Perkins; Old Josh Benson; Cacklin; William (Billy) Budd; Mole; Dawkins; Caroli; Cattermole; Mrs. Gray; Lambert.
